title: Signed residency checkpoints and retention decision engine API for automated audit bundles
creator: Jonah Brooks
description: Design and implement a new API and webhook semantics that create cryptographically signed residency checkpoints and surface retention-decisions for automated audit bundle generation. The goal is to provide callers (internal services and enterprise customers) with an authoritative, time-stamped assertion that: 1) a data object was stored in a specific region at a given time (residency checkpoint), 2) the retention window and state for that object (active, expired, legal hold) as determined by the retention decision engine, and 3) a signed evidence bundle link for downstream auditors. The API must integrate with customer KMS for optional attestation signing, support our HSM-backed signer for platform assertions, and emit webhook events for checkpoint creation, retention-change, and bundle-ready states. Real-time delivery must be best-effort with guaranteed at-least-once semantics and idempotency keys. The system will also produce deterministic audit bundles (zipped, signed manifests, checksums) accessible via presigned links and archived according to retention TTLs and legal-hold overrides.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoint POST /v1/compliance/checkpoints accepts a payload with object_id, region, customer_id, retention_policy_id and returns 202 + signed_checkpoint_url within 500ms under P95 for simple validation paths

Signed checkpoint payload includes issuer, region, timestamp (ISO8601), object_digest (sha256), signer_kid, and signature using platform HSM or customer KMS; signature scheme: ES256K or RSA-PSS as configured

Webhook contract: events "checkpoint.created", "retention.updated", "bundle.available" with idempotency-key header, retry policy (exponential backoff 5 attempts), and delivery status endpoint GET /v1/compliance/delivery-status/:event_id

Retention decision engine resolves policy precedence (customer policy, legal-hold, system-default) and exposes reason_code and TTL in decision field; decisions are traceable via trace_id and stored for 7 years for audit teams

Evidence bundles: created on bundle.available event, contain manifest.json (signed), object checksums, system logs slice (redacted), and a presigned S3/GCS link; bundles must be immutable and retention-anchored

Automated tests and integration: unit tests for signer rotations, end-to-end integration test that validates webhook retries, idempotency, and bundle verification; load test demonstrating 2000 checkpoints/min sustained with 99% success under dedicated capacity
notes: 2026-02-20: Spike completed. Proved HSM signer latency and feasibility of embedding KMS-signed assertion in a compact JWT-like envelope. Notes: /docs/confluence/compliance/checkpoint-spike
2026-02-27: Chose ES256K for default platform signing due to smaller signature size and ECC curve availability on HSM. Trade-off: RSA-PSS supported for customers using legacy KMS keys.
2026-03-03: Decided to implement deterministic bundle manifests (sorted entries, canonical JSON) to simplify signature verification by auditors and to make replay comparisons straightforward.

2026-03-05: Observability spec drafted: metrics: checkpoints_created_total, checkpoints_signed_latency_ms_bucket, webhook_delivery_failures_total, bundles_generated_total; traces must include signer_kid and retention_reason_code.
2026-03-10: Open PR created for the signer service and proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821
2026-03-11: Security review scheduled; initial threat model shows need to harden presigned link TTLs and add optional link-binding claim to the signed manifest.
Operational runbook draft: /runbooks/compliance-checkpoints (contains escalation for webhook delivery spikes and signer rotation procedure).
comments: 2026-02-22 - Jonah Brooks: Spike shows HSM signing adds ~40ms median; acceptable for async webhook body but we should avoid blocking fast paths. Proposal: return 202 and emit checkpoint.created when signing completes.
2026-03-01 - Priya Kapoor: Please add support for legal-hold overrides at decision time and an admin API to release holds. This impacts retention decision engine design.
2026-03-06 - Mateo Alvarez (Security): Customer KMS integration must include proof-of-owner flow; do not accept raw customer public keys without challenge-response.
2026-03-09 - Lina Park (SRE): Add circuit-breaker for webhook destinations exhibiting >10% 5xx in a 5m window to prevent backpressure on the delivery queue.
2026-03-12 - Priya Kapoor: Moved to In Progress. Working on API implementation and integration tests. Blocking: dependency on ENG-61234 for outbound delivery orchestration.
